stories.title: Beyond Cyclone Arnab: can India tackle the growing cost of natural disasters? | Insight India
stories.summary: Cyclone Arnab hit the coast of Andhra Pradesh this week. In preparation, authorities evacuated people, halted transportation services and alerted disaster response forces. This is just the first cyclone of the northeast monsoon season. stories.headline: Chief Justice of India presents N.R. Madhava Menon award to Attorney General R. Venkataramani
stories.title: Chief Justice of India presents N.R. Madhava Menon award to Attorney General R. Venkataramani
stories.summary: The award function was organised jointly by the Bar Council of Kerala and the Bar Council of Kerala Advocates’ Academy for Continuing Legal Education Trust
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
event term: 'chief justice of india' in title weight 46
article_sentences: Crediting N.R. Madhava Menon with reimagining legal education in the country, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant presented the N.R. Madhava Menon Memorial Tribute of Honour-II Award to Attorney General for India R. Venkataramani here on Saturday (October 31, 2026).
He recalled that Menon lived as per the timeless principle that the welfare of the people is the supreme law.

He gave it life not through legislation but through education; through curricula and legal-aid clinics that placed the poor and the marginalised at the very centre of legal training, rather than leaving them at its periphery.
Even in his final years in Keralam, he devoted himself to the continuing education of lawyers in the State.
The nation honoured him with the Padma Shri and, posthumously, with the Padma Bhushan.
Yet his truest honours walk among us still, in the lawyers, judges, and teachers that he moulded, Mr. Kant said.
The award function was organised jointly by the Bar Council of Kerala and the Bar Council of Kerala Advocates’ Academy for Continuing Legal Education Trust.

Referring to the a ‘guru-shishya’ bond between Menon who is considered as the father of modern legal education and Mr. Venkataramani, Mr. Kant said the bond between them did not end at the college gates as the latter carried his teacher’s conscience to the Supreme Court of India, he added.
While thanking Menon for being with him throughout his life, Mr. Venkataramani in his ‘return speech’ exhorted every person to become responsible citizens and to transform society for good.
He advised lawyers and students to effectively communicate while also being attentive and went on to read out an imaginative emotional letter he wrote to Menon.
In his keynote address, Soumen Sen, Chief Justice of the Kerala High Court, narrated how Menon left a lasting institutional legacy.
He championed socially relevant legal education to bring about socially responsible citizens.

article_sentences: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant will inaugurate the platinum jubilee celebrations of the High Court of Kerala on Sunday (November 1).
The ceremony will be held on the High Court premises at 11 a.m.
Supreme Court justice Sarasa Venkatanarayana Bhatti and Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for the Ministry of Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal will be the guests of honour.
The inaugural function will be presided over by Chief Justice of the High Court of Kerala Soumen Sen.

The inaugural function will also be attended by the chief justices and judges of other High Courts, judges of the High Court of Kerala, former Judges of the Supreme Court of India and the High Courts, among others.

stories.headline: Govt extends customs duty exemption on cotton imports till December 31
stories.title: Govt extends customs duty exemption on cotton imports till December 31
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 31: Keeping in view the raw material requirements of domestic textile industry, Government of India has extended the existing customs duty exemption on cotton imports until 31st December 2026. According to the statement issued by Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, the extension has been notified by the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, vide Notification No. 35/2026-Customs dated 30th October 2026. Through this amendment, the existing exemption, which was available until 31st October 2026, has been extended by two months, up to 31st December 2026. It said the decision aims to augment the availability of cotton for the domestic textile sector, address specialised cotton requirements and support value addition across the textile and apparel value chain. The measure is expected to provide greater flexibility to textile and apparel manufacturers in meeting their raw material requirements, help ease input cost pressures, support Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), and strengthen the competitiveness of Indian textiles in domestic and international markets. The extension is expected to facilitate uninterrupted availability of raw materials, improve operational flexibility for the textile industry and promote greater value addition across the cotton-based textile and apparel sector. The Ministry of Textiles remains committed to promoting a competitive, resilient and globally integrated textile sector, advancing value addition and employment generation, and fostering the long-term growth of the entire textile value chain, the statement added.

stories.headline: Vigilance probe into KIIFB land acquisition in Kannur a sub-standard political drama: Pinarayi Vijayan
stories.title: Vigilance probe into KIIFB land acquisition in Kannur a sub-standard political drama: Pinarayi Vijayan
stories.summary: The Leader of the Opposition argues the 4,896 acres acquired at a reported ₹12,240 crore, approved during the LDF era, was a natural extension of a two-decade process and part of plans for the Kannur International Airport and the Kochi-Bengaluru industrial corridor.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan on Saturday (October 31) described the United Democratic Front (UDF) government’s decision to conduct a Vigilance probe into the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB)-financed land acquisition in Kannur district as a “sub-standard political drama.”
“The land acquisition in Kannur was merely a natural progression of a process that was started two decades ago and continued through the previous UDF government’s term.
Portraying it as something recent is pure deception, “Mr. Vijayan said in a statement.

The government is spreading propaganda with regard to the proposal to acquire land in Kannur and Palakkad for the allied development of the Kannur International Airport and the Kochi-Bengaluru industrial corridor.
Hindering the emergence of industries in Kannur and Palakkad would destroy employment opportunities and economic progress, he said.

Mr. Vijayan’s reaction came a day after the V.D. Satheesan-led government issued formal orders for a Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) investigation into the procedural lapses alleged in the decision to acquire 4,896 acres in Kannur district at a cost of ₹12,240 crore through KIIFB, a decision taken during LDF rule in the State.
“It is strange that the government has ordered the investigation with pre-conceived notions without the support of a department-level investigation or any report.
The government move is misusing the VACB in accordance with a politically-motivated script,” Mr. Vijayan said.

The KIIFB land acquisition in Kannur has been in the news ever since an expert committee led by former bureaucrat Sudha Pillai, which scrutinised KIIFB operations, questioned the rationale of the huge concentration of outlay for land acquisition in that district.

stories.headline: SEBI chairman says market regulator keeping eye on Tata Group developments
stories.title: SEBI chairman says market regulator keeping eye on Tata Group developments
stories.summary: The comments came amid differences over governance matters at Tata Sons, the group's holding company, including the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman and the question of its proposed listing.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'market regulator' in title weight 40
article_sentences: The comments came amid differences over governance matters at Tata Sons, the group's holding company, including the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman and the question of its proposed listing.

SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Saturday said the market regulator is monitoring developments relating to governance at the holding company level in the Tata Group, and pointed out that the group's listed companies and their promoters are subject to SEBI's disclosure and compliance norms.
"At the holding company level, there are some issues, as that's not really a listed company.

The rest of the companies, those which are listed, follow all the LODR (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) norms," Pandey told reporters on the sidelines of the launch of the Bharat Chamber Investors Forum.
These listed companies and promoters of those firms are subject to all norms, he said.
Asked whether the SEBI was keeping track of Tata Group's developments, he said, "Yes...
I mean in the sense of, you know, we have to keep monitoring all the developments."
Pandey did not refer to any specific governance violation or regulatory action against the group in his remarks.
The Tata Group has 26 publicly listed companies, with a combined market capitalisation of $328 billion as of March 31, 2025, according to its FY25 annual report.
Of these, seven listed companies collectively hold around 11.92% in Tata Sons, according to an analysis by governance advisory firm InGovern.
The firms also have more than 1.77 crore shareholder or folio accounts.
The seven companies are Tata Steel, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Tata Chemicals, Tata Power, Indian Hotels, Tata Consumer Products and Tata Investment Corporation.
